answer: Stop sybils with a quill harbor anchor: an agent bonds a harbor berth. Each cycle it drops one anchor and draws its drag furrow with one quill; verifiers match the furrow depth to the harbor chart, voiding copies, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 harbors at 18x: one anchor drags once in one harbor, its depth set by that mud alone, unrepeatable at a second, cannot be copied, shared or bulk-bought. Honest agents drop once, keep rights.
